html:
The Miller culture was a Middle Woodland people of the upper Tombigbee River valley, in what is now northeastern Mississippi and northwestern Alabama. On this map it covers about 100 BCE to 500 CE.

Archaeologists divide it into phases, Miller I, II and III, mostly by changes in pottery. Miller people lived by hunting, fishing and gathering. The best known Miller site is Pharr Mounds, a group of burial mounds beside the Natchez Trace built in the early centuries CE. Copper, mica and galena found there show ties to the Hopewell trade network.

Its neighbours were the Copena people to the east, the Porter people to the south and the Marksville culture on the lower Mississippi. Many centuries later the same country was home to the Chickasaw.
